options.label: Hook + skill only (Recommended)
options.description: Changes observe_ground.py, observe-ground.sh, their tests and the /observe skill's End/Rules. record_decision.py stays unchanged. The harness's wrong resume and the split dialog log (asked under one id, answered under another) are named as out of reach.

options.label: Also change record_decision.py
options.description: Also adds a recorder-side remedy for logs written while armed (see the logs question). More surface, and it touches BK-397's D2 design.

options.label: Escape only, no auto-signal
options.description: Only the manual way out. rearm keeps re-arming cleared sessions, so every wrong resume needs the maintainer to act.

questions.question: What tells rearm that a resumed session was cleared? The probe showed disarm runs on /clear in a cloud session (the marker was removed).

options.label: Tombstone from disarm (Recommended)
options.description: On reason: clear, disarm turns the marker into a 'cleared' tombstone instead of deleting it, and rearm leaves a tombstoned session unarmed. Verified path. Limit: the tombstone lives in the container's tmp/, so a resume into a fresh container (logs already lost there) still re-arms.

options.label: Tombstone + clear-start sweep
options.description: Also, at SessionStart with source clear, and only in a cloud session (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE set), tombstone every armed marker. Covers a missed SessionEnd. It assumes one live session per container. Never applied locally, where it would disarm a parallel /observe session (an S2 weakening).

options.label: Transcript marker
options.description: Look for a /clear after the /observe prompt in the transcript. Not in the repo's transcript file: the incident records the clear only as a conversation_reset stream event (10ba6e13). Unverified, likely absent.

questions.question: How does a wrongly armed session get out, and what may a cleared or released session do?

options.label: /observe release, record locked (Recommended)
options.description: The maintainer types /observe release. The arm hook turns the marker into the same tombstone, so later restarts honour it. A tombstoned session may do anything except Write/Edit its entry's record, so nothing written into the record follows reads off the ground (keeps S2, S4). The model cannot release itself. Every refusal names the way out. Trade-off: a rightful resume of a cleared session cannot continue the record and needs a fresh /observe.

options.label: /observe release, fully unarmed
options.description: Same trigger, but the tombstoned session is unrestricted, record included, as after today's disarm. Simpler. It weakens S4: a released session could edit the record after reading 0.33 code.

options.label: Neutral ReadNotifications only
options.description: No release. Peers can reach an armed session, but it still cannot commit or read off the ground. It opens a channel for 0.33 content around S1 and does not fix the logs.

questions.question: How do decision logs written while wrongly armed reach the repo?

options.label: Session commits after release (Recommended)
options.description: Once released, the session has Bash and commits its own logs. The skill's End and the refusal text say so. No recorder change. Bound: a container archived before release still loses them, and the split of one dialog across two session ids is the harness's doing.

options.label: Armed git-commit allowlist
options.description: An armed session may run one exact command that commits and pushes sdd/decisions/ only. That saves logs even without release, but it opens Bash in an armed session, and git and pre-commit output can carry repo content (S1/S2 surface).

options.label: Warn at SessionStart
options.description: rearm prints the uncommitted decision logs whenever it arms or locks a session, so the maintainer sees what is at risk. This adds a notice, not a fix.

PR #1189 has hit the /ship soft limit of 5 finding rounds. Findings per round: 2, 3, 8, 4, 4. Rounds 1, 2 and 4 found behaviour bugs: a released locked session could write any record, MultiEdit got through, a release before the first tool use locked the session, another entry's record was writable, and the lock notice lacked the way out. Its measuring member re-ran every writer against every path form for four release sources, and 115 tests passed. options.description: Same three members as round 5 (unprimed, measuring, whole-file). Costs one more measuring run, roughly 5 minutes of agent time, for a pass over a commit that changes no code.

questions.question: The verification pass on #1189 found a real gap in the round-2 fix. When a session resumes in a new container, or under a new session id, no marker exists, so rearm re-arms from the transcript. It honours an `/observe release` only if that prompt came before the session's first tool use. A real session's first action is the canary Read, so a maintainer's release always comes later and is ignored: the released session re-arms on every such restart, and the maintainer must type /observe release again each time. The test hid this by putting the release before the first tool use, an order no real transcript has. How should it be fixed?

options.label: Honour release anywhere (Recommended)
options.description: rearm treats an `/observe release` user prompt anywhere after the arming prompt as ending the arming, so the resume stays unarmed with no repeat release. Only typed user prompts count (tool results and meta entries are already skipped). This shrinks the docstring's 'cannot do' list. Test first, using the realistic order (arm, tool use, release).

options.label: Drop the dead branch
options.description: Remove the before-first-tool-use release check and its test. Keep today's behaviour: a new-container or new-id resume re-arms, and the maintainer types /observe release again. Smaller change, and the docstring already describes that limit.

questions.question: This would be the 7th review pass (5 finding rounds plus a verification pass, both over the soft limit). Rounds went 2, 3, 8, 4, 4, 4 findings. Behaviour bugs came in rounds 1, 2, 4 and now the verification pass, and this one sits in code the loop itself added. After this fix, how should the loop end?

options.label: Measuring + unprimed pass (Recommended)
options.description: Two fresh reviewers on the fix commit: one runs the hook against the realistic transcripts, one reads with no briefing. If both are clean, I close, paste the review block and write the report. If not, I come back to you.

options.label: Close after the fix
options.description: Fix, run the gate, push, then close without another review. The record will note the final fix pass as unreviewed, a waiver you made.
